newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit down slightly, seen confined to thin range.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit down slightly, seen confined to thin range.

text.p: The ringgit was marginally lower against the dollar in late Kuala Lumpur trading as activity thinned substantially due to a lack of interest, dealers said on Tuesday.
They said the ringgit was expected to remain confined to a narrow trading range, held there by a weak dollar, positive Malaysian economic data and corporate dollar demand.

"Ringgit is weak in the afternoon because of some stop/loss (dollar) sales by London-based players. The volumes are extremely low," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank. "The near-trend depends on where dollar/majors will go," he added.
Some dealers said they expected a stronger ringgit after it broke through key resistance level against the Singapore dollar at 0.5550, though it was trading higher later.
"At the current levels, I see a stronger ringgit. Many may re-establish their ringgit/Sing positions. It (long ringgit) is a positive carry," another Malaysian bank dealer said.
Earlier, the ringgit slipped back after overnight gains in London due to Malaysia's surprise September trade surplus.
At 0900 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5214/24 a dollar against 2.5178/88 previously. The Singapore dollar was at 0.5550/55 a ringgit against 0.5554/60. - Madhav Reddy (603-230 8911)
